# Happy Renters, Better Performance: Why Resident Experience Matters Most in Today’s Market


Residents satisfied with their move-in are 31% more likely to renew their leases, underscoring the importance of early experiences in driving long-term property performance


New offering delivers personalization, financial benefits, and ease for residents while solving compliance and operational challenges for property managers


[(opens in a new tab)](https://www.facebook.com/AppFolio/)


[(opens in a new tab)](https://x.com/appfolio)


[(opens in a new tab)](https://www.linkedin.com/company/appfolio)


**Santa Barbara, Calif., April 24, 2026** —[AppFolio](http://www.appfolioinc.com/) (NASDAQ:APPF), the technology leader powering the future of the real estate industry, today released its 2026 Renter Preferences Report. With 55% of property managers citing vacancy as their[top threat](https://www.appfolio.com/newsroom/property-manager-benchmark-survey-2026) , AppFolio’s[2026 Renter Preferences Report](https://www.appfolio.com/blog/renter-preferences) finds the modern resident experience, driven by convenience and property manager responsiveness, is now table stakes for maintaining occupancy and driving[performance](https://www.appfolio.com/newsroom/appfolio-introduces-real-estate-performance-management) .


As rent growth slows, resident satisfaction is increasingly important for sustaining occupancy, increasing retention, and delivering consistent performance. The report shows that satisfied residents are 72% more likely to renew and 34% less likely to plan a move.


### **Establishing Resident Trust Starts on Day One**


AppFolio’s research identifies the resident move-in as a key opportunity for property managers to improve the resident experience at a critical moment. Residents satisfied with their move-in are 31% more likely to plan to renew their lease, making a friction-free move-in a strong predictor of long-term resident retention.


To capitalize on this opportunity, leading property managers are prioritizing services that take the pain out of moving, along with clear, transparent pricing. By automating essential move-in steps like insurance verification and utility setup, property managers remove day-one friction, creating a better resident experience.


### **Convenience Is No Longer a Differentiator, It’s Expected**


Property managers can more effectively attract new residents by prioritizing valuable services that offer convenience and financial value. Demand for these services is high; 78% of residents say they are an important consideration when evaluating a new home, and 79% are willing to pay for offerings that provide convenience and financial empowerment, yet only 33% can rely on their property managers for access.


When residents do have access to these services, the impact is clear. Residents with financial services score 14% higher on the Cantril Ladder for life satisfaction, and 97% of those with group-rate internet report saving money and improving their financial health.


### **Turning Maintenance Excellence into Resident Advocacy**


While move-in sets the tone, maintenance sustains the relationship. The report highlights that maintenance satisfaction is a critical lever for property performance: residents who are happy with their repairs are 81% more likely to renew and three times more likely to recommend their property manager. By leveraging automation and agentic AI to manage everything from intake to vendor coordination, leading operators are removing the friction from the maintenance process and accelerating the speed of repairs.


### **Driving Better Outcomes Through a Unified Experience**


AppFolio empowers property managers to evolve from managing isolated tasks to driving performance across the entire real estate ecosystem, unifying workflows to unlock long-term value for every stakeholder. By integrating resident services directly into its Performance Platform, AppFolio helps teams deliver seamless experiences that today’s renters expect.


"Property management has always been about more than providing space. Today, it’s about delivering the right experience and value to residents. There is a clear divide between managers who are maintaining operations and those achieving real performance. By leveraging a unified Performance Platform to deliver the digital-first services residents expect, leading operators are turning resident satisfaction into a predictable driver of retention.”


Stacy Holden


Vice President, Industry Principal at AppFolio


[2026 Renter Preferences Report](https://www.appfolio.com/blog/renter-preferences)


**The Cantril Ladder is a long-standing measurement of life satisfaction used by the polling firm Gallup. It assesses how people evaluate their lives, with 0 representing the lowest point and 10 the highest.*


Survey Methodology


AppFolio commissioned a survey of 3,002 U.S. renters ages 18 and up from January 26, 2026 to February 4, 2026.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What Maintenance Response Time Standards Should Property Managers Target, and How Do Top Operators Hit Them Consistently?


Leading operators work toward three standards:


-


Acknowledge every non-emergency request within one to two hours.


-


Resolve it within 24 hours when parts and access allow.


-


Fix it right the first time.


Note that emergencies such as no heat, active leaks, or safety hazards should get an immediate response, around the clock.


And the stakes are clear. According to the


[AppFolio 2026 Renter Preferences Report](https://www.appfolio.com/blog/renter-preferences-report-2026)


, residents satisfied with maintenance are 81% more likely to renew and three times more likely to recommend their property manager.


### How Does the Move-In Experience Impact Long-Term Resident Retention, and What Does a Strong Move-In Process Look Like in 2026?


Move-in sets the baseline for the entire rental experience. The


found that residents satisfied with their move-in are 31% more likely to plan to renew. That makes move-in one of the earliest predictors of retention you have.


A frictionless move-in happens in three stages:


-


**Before day one.** Automate the essentials: digital lease signing, renters insurance verification, utility setup, and resident portal activation. Send one clear welcome message with everything the resident needs, including access instructions, parking, trash schedules, and how to request maintenance.


-


**On day one.** The unit is ready, the keys or access codes work, and the resident can record the unit's condition digitally in minutes.


-


**The first 30 days.** Check in early, around day three and again at day 30. Resolve any move-in issue fast, ideally within 48 hours. A small problem fixed quickly builds more trust than a perfect move-in the resident never thinks about again.


### What Communication Practices Have the Largest Measurable Impact on Resident Satisfaction and Renewal Rates?


The practices that move satisfaction most are the ones that keep residents informed without making them ask.


-


**Offering one channel for everything.** A single online portal lets residents submit requests, pay rent, and track progress, so nothing gets lost across email, voicemail, or sticky notes.


-


**Confirming receipt immediately.** Every request gets an acknowledgment and a realistic time frame.


-


**Updating at every milestone.** Send a message when the visit is scheduled, when parts are ordered, when the technician is on the way, and when the work is complete.


-


**Closing the loop.** A quick satisfaction check after each repair catches problems before they reach the renewal decision.


-


**Announcing community impacts early.** Water shutoffs, pest treatments, and construction notices belong in residents' inboxes days ahead, not on the door that morning.


The


shows that responsiveness and convenience are now table stakes. Communication is where residents feel both.


### How Can Property Management Companies Use AI to Understand Resident Satisfaction?


AI can identify residents who may be trending toward a move-out by surfacing patterns across signals your platform already captures:


-


Changes in payment timing


-


Frequency of maintenance requests and repeat repairs


-


Tone of recent service interactions


-


Where each lease sits in its term


The point isn't to score residents. It's to find fixable problems while there's still time to address them. Effective interventions include:


-


Closing out open maintenance issues


-


A call from the community manager


-


Asking directly about plans and preferences


-


An early renewal conversation with clear options


The


shows why early intervention pays off. Satisfied residents are 72% more likely to renew and 34% less likely to plan a move. The most useful window to act is roughly 60 to 90 days before renewal.


### How Does AI Help Surface Resident Trends?


The fastest-growing opportunity is a gap between what residents want and what they can get. According to the


:


-


78% of residents say services offering convenience and financial value are an important consideration when choosing a new home.


-


79% are willing to pay for those services.


-


Only 33% can currently access them through their property manager.


Residents who do have access report real benefits. Those with financial services score 14% higher on the


[Cantril Ladder](https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/happiness-cantril-ladder)


for life satisfaction. And 97% of residents with group-rate internet report saving money and improving their financial health.


Services residents value in 2026 include:


-


Group-rate internet


-


Renters insurance


-


Rent reporting that helps build credit


-


Package lockers


-


Tiered parking


-


Storage


-


Pet amenities


The operators seeing the strongest results frame these services as choices. Residents understand what each one costs and what they get, and they opt in to what fits their lives.


AI supports this by analyzing uptake, usage, and resident feedback. As a result, you can see which services residents actually value and which bundles might make sense.


### What Is the Actual Financial Cost of Resident Turnover, and How Do Satisfaction Improvements Translate to NOI?


Every move-out carries costs that may go uncounted:


-


Vacancy loss


-


Make-ready labor and materials


-


Marketing


-


Leasing team time


-


Concessions to fill the unit


Industry estimates commonly place the total around


[$4,000](https://naahq.org/news/survey-data-shows-several-disconnects-between-property-managers-and-renters)


per turn, depending on market and unit type.


The math is straightforward: units × renewal rate improvement × cost per turn = annual savings.


For a 200-unit portfolio, a five-point improvement in renewal rate means 10 fewer move-outs a year. At about $4,000 per turn, that preserves roughly $40,000 annually. Those avoided costs flow directly to net operating income (NOI). At a 5% cap rate, that NOI supports roughly $800,000 in added property value.


The


shows where the improvement comes from:


-


Satisfied residents are 72% more likely to renew.


-


Residents satisfied with maintenance are 81% more likely to renew.


-


Residents satisfied with their move-in are 31% more likely to plan to renew.


### How Do Resident Services, Such as Rent Reporting, Group-Rate Internet, and Renters Insurance Bundles, Improve Resident Retention and Satisfaction?


Financial empowerment services turn the lease into something that improves a resident's financial life, not just a monthly payment. The


quantifies the impact:


-


Residents with services score 14% higher on the Cantril Ladder, Gallup's long-standing measure of life satisfaction.


-


97% of residents with group-rate internet report saving money and improving their financial health.


Each service delivers a clear resident benefit:


-


Rent reporting helps residents build credit with a payment they already make.


-


Group-rate internet lowers a monthly bill and simplifies move-in.


-


Renters insurance bundles make coverage simpler to secure and verify.


The demand is there, and so is the gap. 79% of residents are willing to pay for services that offer convenience and financial empowerment, but only 33% can access them through their property manager. Operators who close that gap earn goodwill and give residents another reason to stay.


### What Does a Strong Lease Renewal Process Look Like, and What Do Residents Expect When a Renewal Window Opens?


Residents expect the renewal to feel like a conversation, not a deadline. The strongest renewal processes share five traits:


-


They start early. Reach out 90 to 120 days before lease end, or earlier if local notice rules require it. Last-minute offers force rushed decisions and invite residents to shop around.


-


They fix open issues first. Close outstanding maintenance requests before the offer goes out. An unresolved repair can undo a good offer.


-


They explain the rate. Give a clear, honest reason for any change, and offer term options where possible.


-


They're digital. Residents should be able to review, compare, and sign their renewal online in minutes.


-


They recognize loyalty. Small gestures for long-tenured residents go a long way, such as a unit refresh, a carpet cleaning, or an upgrade.


The payoff is measurable. The


found that satisfied residents are 72% more likely to renew.


### What Capabilities Should Property Managers Look for in a Resident Experience Platform, and How Do They Connect to Measurable Financial Performance?


Resident experience outcomes depend on the technology behind them. When maintenance, communication, payments, and resident services live in disconnected tools, the gaps show up as slow repairs, missed messages, and residents who don't renew.


When you evaluate a platform, look for six capabilities and the outcomes they drive:


-


One unified data model, so every team sees the same resident history. This drives faster, more informed service.


-


Maintenance workflows with AI operating under human monitoring and supervision, from intake to vendor coordination. These improve time to resolve and first-time fix rate.


-


A single resident portal for requests, payments, and communication. This drives satisfaction and fewer escalations.


-


Embedded resident services, such as group-rate internet, renters insurance, and rent reporting. These improve satisfaction and retention.


-


Renewal and retention analytics that surface risk early. These improve renewal rates.


-


Built-in governance, including role-based permissions and other key controls. This supports consistent, streamlined operations.


Then ask the vendor one question: can you connect these capabilities to measurable changes in renewal rate, turnover cost, and NOI?
